paren.romanization.test: the group follows a Hebrew word (one space allowed) and opens on a non-Hebrew character
paren.romanization.means: the romanization of the Hebrew word just before it, sometimes with that word's gloss in curly quotes: (av), (khamishá, “five”)

paren.lead_label.test: the group opens the route, text follows it, and it is not a subject pronoun
paren.lead_label.means: a context label over the whole line: (intransitive), (uncertain), (of celestial bodies); the line ships whole (see refusals)

paren.trailing_label.test: the group ends the route (a '.' may follow), stands after a depth-0 sentence period, and opens lowercase
paren.trailing_label.means: a context label written after the gloss, over the whole line: To leaven, ferment. (of dough); the line ships whole, as under a lead label

paren.trailing_note.test: the group ends the route (a '.' may follow), stands after a depth-0 sentence period, and opens uppercase
paren.trailing_note.means: a note on the whole line: (See usage note below.), (In the construct state); divided off as a note piece, never a reading

paren.subject_pronoun.test: the group holds only he, she, it, they, we, you, I (slash-joined) or And
paren.subject_pronoun.means: the subject pronoun, or the rendering of the prefixed vav, inside a verb-form gloss: (he/it) went, (And) (she/it) brought; part of the reading

paren.nested.test: the group opens inside another parenthesis
paren.nested.means: notation inside the outer note: a romanization, an aside or an example within it

paren.mark_display.test: the group holds a dotted circle or nothing but marks
paren.mark_display.means: displays a Hebrew point on its own: (ִ◌ָ)

paren.hebrew_note.test: the group (not a romanization) holds Hebrew letters
paren.hebrew_note.means: a usage note citing Hebrew: (see also צליל), (sometimes followed by מֵת), (with לְ־ (l'-))

paren.argument_slot.test: the group holds only an argument word: someone, something, oneself, a person (optionally after a preposition)
paren.argument_slot.means: the verb's object or argument slot inside one reading: to make (someone) laugh

paren.grammar_label.test: the group names a conjugation in a form-of line: (suffix conjugation), (hence past tense)
paren.grammar_label.means: a grammatical label inside a form pointer

paren.qualifier.test: any other balanced group at depth 0
paren.qualifier.means: a qualifier or sense description on the English it follows (translation-table style): father (a male parent, ...), to close (window, door, shutter); never a second reading

paren.unclosed_opener.means: a truncated or damaged note; from it onward nothing divides (the August opener_never_closed rule)

bracket.government.means: the preposition or particle the Hebrew word governs: [with מִן (mín) or מִ־ (mí-)]

bracket.cross_reference.means: a cross-reference to a usage note: [see usage note regarding the plural]

bracket.wiki_markup.test: the route carries '[[' (a wiki link the export did not render)
bracket.wiki_markup.means: wiki link markup left in the text: [[[in order that|in order]]]

bracket.elision.test: the bracket holds only an ellipsis

bracket.supplied_word.test: the bracket holds one or two lowercase English words
bracket.supplied_word.means: an optional English word inside one reading: the other side [of]

bracket.phonetic.test: the bracket holds a short form carrying a combining mark

semicolon.sense_boundary.test: outside every scope; the next segment does not open as a note
semicolon.sense_boundary.means: divides one sense group from the next: to blossom, bloom; to flourish

semicolon.note_follows.test: outside every scope; the next segment opens as a note (used, see, said of, indicating, also, for example, in full, it, this, ...)
semicolon.note_follows.means: divides the glosses from a usage note that follows them; the note is kept whole as its own piece (an aside, not a reading)

period.before_trailing_note.test: a depth-0 period followed only by a parenthetical group that opens uppercase
period.before_trailing_note.means: ends the gloss before a note on the whole line: ... to terminate. (See usage note below.); the note is its own piece (role note)

period.sentence_boundary.test: outside every scope, followed by a space and an uppercase letter, '(' or a quote, and the word before it is not an abbreviation
period.sentence_boundary.means: ends one sentence of the gloss and starts another (usually a note: 'Also known as ...', '(See usage note below.)'); divides like a semicolon

colon.head_explanation.test: outside every scope, text on both sides, neither part carries Hebrew outside parentheses
colon.head_explanation.means: divides the head gloss(es) from the explanation that defines them: A tunnel: an underground or underwater passage; the explanation is kept whole as one piece

colon.pointer_gloss.test: outside every scope, text on both sides, the part before carries Hebrew letters outside parentheses (a form pointer)
colon.pointer_gloss.means: divides a form pointer from the English glosses of that form: plural indefinite form of כּוֹס (kos): cups, glasses, tumblers; the part after it is a reading list

colon.gloss_pointer.test: outside every scope, text on both sides, the part before carries no Hebrew outside parentheses and the part after does (a form pointer)
colon.gloss_pointer.means: divides the gloss from the form pointer that gives its grammar: (he/it) went: third-person masculine singular ... of הָלַךְ (halákh); the pointer is its own piece (role pointer), never a reading

colon.strongs_list.test: outside every scope and followed by ' - ' or ' – ' (Strong's ':-')
colon.strongs_list.means: a Strong's entry copied into Wiktionary: divides the definition from Strong's KJV rendering list, which is kept whole

comma.gloss_boundary.test: outside every scope, in a part (head, explanation or post-pointer) with no Hebrew outside parentheses and not in a note, and no comma of that part is a label, etc., clause, conjunction or relative comma
comma.gloss_boundary.means: alternation: divides one English gloss from the next (Wiktionary's synonym list): defect, deficiency, blemish

semicolon.in_parentheses.means: divides senses inside a parenthetical description; the parenthesis is one note

semicolon.under_lead_label.test: outside every scope in a route led by a context label
semicolon.under_lead_label.means: a sense boundary under a label that governs the whole line; held (the route ships whole)

period.terminal.means: ends the gloss; part of the last piece

period.in_parentheses.means: an abbreviation, a decimal point or the note's own sentence end, inside the note

period.ellipsis.means: an ellipsis written as dots: what is ...?, a slot for a word

period.abbreviation.test: outside every scope, not terminal, and either the word before it is an abbreviation (e.g., U.S.S.R., St.) or punctuation follows it directly
period.abbreviation.means: the period of an abbreviation inside a run: e.g. by paying a fee; St., st., street

period.lowercase_continuation.test: outside every scope, followed by a space and a lowercase letter, the word before it not an abbreviation
period.lowercase_continuation.means: a sentence end the provider continued in lowercase; held, not divided (3 occurrences; see open questions)

period.under_lead_label.test: a sentence boundary in a route led (or, after its last period, closed) by a context label

colon.in_parentheses.means: head/explanation or citation inside a parenthetical note

colon.introduces_absent_list.test: nothing follows it in its segment
colon.introduces_absent_list.means: introduces sub-senses this route does not carry: to be:, Possibilities include:

colon.under_lead_label.test: outside every scope in a route led by a context label

comma.in_parentheses.means: notation inside a parenthetical: a list of objects (window, door, shutter), a romanization and its gloss (khamishá, “five”), or the note's own prose

comma.trailing.test: nothing but whitespace follows it in its part
comma.trailing.means: a comma closing a truncated list; no piece follows

comma.under_lead_label.test: outside every scope in a route led by a context label

comma.pointer.test: outside every scope in a part that carries Hebrew letters outside parentheses
comma.pointer.means: inside a form pointer: plural indefinite form of X (x), defective spelling; ... of X, with a first-person singular pronoun suffix

comma.in_note.test: outside every scope in a segment that opens as a note (used, see, said of, indicating, also, it, this, ...)
comma.in_note.means: inside a usage note's own sentence: What; used in forming exclamations, may be used to express ...; the note is held whole

comma.strongs_list.test: outside every scope after a Strong's ': -'
comma.strongs_list.means: Strong's KJV list comma; the list is held whole (see open questions)

comma.after_label.test: the first piece of the part is a label (figuratively, specifically, by extension, ...) and the next piece runs two words or more, or the first piece opens with a one-word label or a parenthesis
comma.after_label.means: follows a label that governs the rest of the part: figuratively, to perceive; the part is held whole

comma.before_etc.means: the list is open-ended inside one phrase: to board (a plane), to enter (a street via a junction), etc.; the part is held whole

comma.before_clause.test: the next piece runs two words or more and opens with especially, such, usually, used, equivalent, e.g., i.e., representing, transliterated, ... (unless the first piece is a one- or two-word function-word gloss)
comma.before_clause.means: opens a qualifying clause: song, singing, especially traditional ...; the part is a sentence and is held whole

comma.before_serial_conjunction.test: the next piece runs two words or more and opens with or, and, nor, but (unless the first piece is a one- or two-word function-word gloss)
comma.before_serial_conjunction.means: the last item of an enumeration inside one phrase: any of Passover, Shavuot, Sukkot, or Shemini Atzeret; the part is held whole

comma.before_relative.test: the next piece runs two words or more and opens with as, like, that, which, who, whose, where, when, from, about, rather, hence, ... while the part's first piece opens on a content word
comma.before_relative.means: attaches a relative or comparative clause to the gloss before it: A destination, as of a voyage; a male given name, Aziz, from Arabic; the part is held whole

comma.shared_object.test: the piece before it is one or two words ending on a preposition (not a 'to' infinitive), the part's first piece is such a piece, and its last piece opens with or/and and does not end on a preposition
comma.shared_object.means: the pieces share one object written once at the end: of, pertaining to, or being the descendants of Jacob; the part is held whole

comma.before_bare_group.test: the next piece is nothing but one parenthetical group
comma.before_bare_group.means: the group qualifies the gloss before it and is no reading of its own: chicken, (female); Wren, (Troglodytes troglodytes); the part is held whole

comma.list_inside_sentence.test: a gloss-shaped comma in a part that carries one of the holding commas above
comma.list_inside_sentence.means: an item boundary of a list inside a sentence: To bring in, take in, send in, or otherwise cause ...; held with its sentence

hyphen.romanization.means: marks a bound prefix or compound in the romanization: (mi-), (sákh-hakól)

hyphen.strongs_list_marker.test: follows ':' (and a space) and precedes a space
hyphen.strongs_list_marker.means: the dash of Strong's ':-' that opens the KJV rendering list

hyphen.strongs_suffix.test: after a Strong's ':-' in the same route, opening a suffix
hyphen.strongs_suffix.means: Strong's suffix notation inside the KJV list: (-r, over), chief (-est)

hyphen.range.test: between two digits, or spaced between two dates or numbers
hyphen.range.means: a range: 8-6th centuries, Psalms 113-118, April 21 - May 21

hyphen.compound.test: between two letters or digits (or after ')' before a letter)
hyphen.compound.means: joins a compound word: third-person, living room-kitchen, 24-hour, pre-1948

hyphen.bound_prefix_gloss.test: ends a word (letter before, space, punctuation or end after)
hyphen.bound_prefix_gloss.means: the gloss is an English prefix, or a suspended compound: pre-, Single-, cup- or trumpet-shaped

hyphen.bound_suffix_gloss.test: opens a word (start, space or '(' before, letter after)
hyphen.bound_suffix_gloss.means: the gloss is an English suffix: -less, -ie, -able

hyphen.spaced_dash.test: a space on both sides, not after a colon, not between numbers or dates
hyphen.spaced_dash.means: a dash introducing an apposition inside one reading: a 'kibbutz' - a collective settlement

slash.spelling_pair.test: Hebrew on both sides (a space allowed)
slash.spelling_pair.means: separates the unpointed and pointed spellings of one cited Hebrew lemma: קובל / קֻבַּל

slash.alternation_in_reading.test: letters on both sides, no space
slash.alternation_in_reading.means: packs alternatives inside one reading's shared frame: happy is/was/will be, Screw him/her/it!; dividing would leave fragments ('happy is')

slash.alternation_spaced.test: a space on at least one side, English on both
slash.alternation_spaced.means: alternative words inside one reading or note: Jewish feast / festival / holiday

maqaf.hebrew.test: next to a Hebrew letter or point
maqaf.hebrew.means: the Hebrew hyphen of a cited bound form or compound: מִ־, סַךְ־הַכֹּל

maqaf.named.test: not next to a Hebrew letter
maqaf.named.means: the maqaf character itself, named by the gloss: the Hebrew script hyphen (־)

hebrew_point.on_letter.test: follows a Hebrew letter or another point
hebrew_point.on_letter.means: a vowel point, dagesh or shin/sin dot of a cited Hebrew form

hebrew_point.mark_display.test: next to a dotted circle or alone in a display parenthesis
hebrew_point.mark_display.means: the point shown on its own, as the thing the entry names

dotted_circle.carrier.means: the dotted circle that carries a displayed point

geresh.hebrew.means: geresh: an abbreviation mark or a foreign-sound mark on a Hebrew letter (ז׳, נפ׳)

gershayim.hebrew.test: follows a Hebrew letter or point
gershayim.hebrew.means: gershayim: the acronym mark inside a Hebrew word (שד״ר)

gershayim.named.means: the gershayim character named by the gloss

apostrophe.romanization.means: a glottal stop or shva in the romanization: (n'kevá), ('ír)

apostrophe.word_internal.means: English elision or possessive: one's, doesn't, y'all

apostrophe.word_final.means: plural possessive or a closing single quote: brides' parents, Tuqu'

apostrophe.opening_quote.means: an opening single quote: a 'kibbutz', also called 'Zaccur'

straight_double.gershayim_substitute.means: an ASCII quote standing for gershayim in a romanized acronym: Shu"m

straight_double.quotation.test: one of a pair in the route
straight_double.quotation.means: quotation marks around a quoted gloss or term: ("quail"), "Lady of the night"

straight_double.named_character.test: the route's quotes do not pair and this one is left over
straight_double.named_character.means: the double-quote character named by the gloss

curly_double.romanization_gloss.means: quotes the gloss of the cited Hebrew word: (khamishá, “five”)

curly_double.quotation.means: quotation marks around a quoted meaning or phrase

curly_single.apostrophe.means: an apostrophe typed as a curly quote: one’s

curly_single.particle_gloss.means: quotes the gloss of the governed particle: [with ל־ (l'-) ‘to’]

exclamation.terminal.means: ends an interjection or imperative gloss; part of the reading: Wow!, move!

question.terminal.means: ends a question gloss; part of the reading: Is it true?

en_dash.range.test: digits or dates on both sides

en_dash.strongs_list_marker.means: the dash of Strong's ':–' list marker

em_dash.range_or_aside.means: a range (879 — 912 CE) or a parenthetical dash inside one reading

ellipsis.slot_or_truncation.means: an elided slot or a cut-off passage: והאופנים…, still, …

plus.composition.means: composition in a grammatical note: את + ה־, (+ activity)

equals.expansion.means: introduces the full form an abbreviation stands for: =לירה ישראלית, [=Jonathan]

symbol.named_or_shown.means: the symbol itself, shown or named by the gloss; the Hebrew word names the symbol (tilde, spade, dagger, number sign)

symbol.notation.means: notation inside one reading: a fraction slash, a unit dot (N·m), percent, a times sign, an ion charge, an IPA diacritic, an ampersand, grapheme brackets <th>

wiki_template.residue.means: a wiki template the export did not render: ({{taxlink|Citrus × aurantium f
